history: Created in 1889 for Queen Margherita to represent Italy's flag colors: red (tomato), white (mozzarella), green (basil).
ingredients: Pizza dough, San Marzano tomatoes, fresh mozzarella, basil, olive oil
preparation: 1. Stretch dough. 2. Add tomato sauce. 3. Top with mozzarella. 4. Bake in wood oven. 5. Add fresh basil.
description: The iconic Neapolitan pizza showcasing perfect simplicity: wood-fired crust, vibrant tomato sauce, fresh mozzarella, and basil. A culinary tribute to Italy's flag and the queen of pizzas.

history: Originated in Lazio region as a way to showcase regional cheese varieties in one dish.
ingredients: Pizza dough, mozzarella, gorgonzola, parmesan, fontina (or other local cheeses)
preparation: 1. Stretch dough. 2. Arrange cheeses in sections. 3. Bake until cheeses melt and bubble.
description: A luxurious blend of four premium cheeses melting into perfect harmony on crisp pizza dough. Each bite delivers a symphony of creamy, tangy, and sharp flavors for true cheese connoisseurs.

history: Created in mid-20th century Rome, named 'capricious' for its varied toppings chosen by chef's whim.
ingredients: Pizza dough, tomato, mozzarella, ham, mushrooms, artichokes, olives, egg
preparation: 1. Spread tomato base. 2. Add mozzarella. 3. Arrange other toppings. 4. Bake. 5. Add egg last minutes.
description: The 'capricious' pizza featuring an artful arrangement of ham, mushrooms, artichokes, and olives crowned with a baked egg. A flavorful mosaic that changes with every bite.

history: Southern Italian pizza created to showcase spicy salami ('diavola' means 'devil' for its heat).
ingredients: Pizza dough, tomato, mozzarella, spicy salami, chili flakes, olive oil
preparation: 1. Spread tomato base. 2. Add mozzarella. 3. Top with salami. 4. Sprinkle chili. 5. Bake.
description: For those who like it hot! This fiery pizza features spicy salami and chili flakes on a tomato base - a devilishly good combination that lives up to its name with bold, intense flavors.

history: Ancient Ligurian bread dating to Roman times, originally cooked on hearth stones.
ingredients: Flour, water, yeast, olive oil, salt, rosemary
preparation: 1. Make dough. 2. Let rise. 3. Dimple surface. 4. Drench with olive oil. 5. Bake until golden.
description: Liguria's signature olive oil-rich bread with its characteristic dimpled surface. Perfectly crisp outside and pillowy inside, often fragrant with rosemary - a simple yet sublime Italian staple.

history: Traditional Romagna street food dating to Byzantine era, originally made with lard instead of oil.
ingredients: Flour, lard (or olive oil), water, salt, filling (cheese, cured meats, greens)
preparation: 1. Make thin dough. 2. Cook on griddle. 3. Fill with ingredients. 4. Fold and serve warm.
description: Emilia-Romagna's answer to the flatbread sandwich - warm, slightly chewy unleavened bread folded around delicious fillings. The ultimate portable Italian comfort food with endless variations.

history: Ancient Sardinian shepherds' bread that could last for months during long periods tending flocks.
ingredients: Durum wheat flour, yeast, salt, water
preparation: 1. Make thin dough. 2. Bake briefly. 3. Separate layers. 4. Re-bake until crisp.
description: Sardinia's famous 'music paper bread' - incredibly thin, crisp sheets with a delicate texture. This ingenious preservation method created a durable yet delicious bread perfect for pairing with cheeses and meats.

history: Roman specialty originally sold by weight as a snack, without toppings to highlight quality olive oil.
ingredients: Pizza dough, olive oil, rosemary, sea salt
preparation: 1. Stretch dough. 2. Bake plain. 3. Brush with olive oil. 4. Sprinkle salt and herbs.
description: Rome's minimalist masterpiece - crusty pizza dough brushed with finest olive oil and sprinkled with sea salt. The ultimate test of a pizzaiolo's skill, letting quality ingredients shine in their simplicity.
